about: Every voiced line of marrow.ink: who speaks it and the exact words. tools/lines.mjs --check voices.json proves this file matches the ink. Each line has two takes, media/vo/<id>-1.mp3 and -2.mp3, made with eleven_v3; the page plays one at random.

p1-open.speaker: narrator
p1-open.text: The Steeple Wyke Horticultural Show, the hundred and twelfth. You have been a detective sergeant in this county for nineteen days.

p10-open.speaker: narrator
p10-open.text: Sunday. The marquee is coming down, and the marrows have gone to the pig farm.

p10a-1.speaker: narrator
p10a-1.text: Men in shorts are folding the marquee. The Pike Cup is in a box marked Village Hall, Do Not Remove.

p10b-1.speaker: narrator
p10b-1.text: Margaret has cut one foxglove, and is putting it in a vase on the kitchen table.

p10b-2.speaker: margaret
p10b-2.text: Thank you, Sergeant. You were very thorough. They look nice indoors, as long as nobody drinks the water.

p10c-1.speaker: narrator
p10c-1.text: Quaile has taken her hearing aid out. It is on the dashboard.

p10c-2.speaker: quaile
p10c-2.text: You did well, Sam. For nineteen days.

p10c-4.speaker: quaile
p10c-4.text: Hm? Other side, Sam. That one's off.

p10d-1.speaker: narrator
p10d-1.text: The scarecrows are still along the hedge. The straw vicar has gone.

p10d-2.speaker: narrator
p10d-2.text: At the end of the row is a new one: a navy mac, a loose tie, brown city shoes, a small black notebook. Its card says Our Village, D S Adeyemi.

p10d-3.speaker: quaile
p10d-3.text: Twenty days, and they've made you already. That's quick.

p1a-1.speaker: narrator
p1a-1.text: Bunting, a marquee, a brass band from the next village, and four hundred people who know each other's business.

p1a-2.speaker: narrator
p1a-2.text: Behind the marquee, a church spire. In front of it, a line of scarecrows.

p1b-1.speaker: quaile
p1b-1.text: You came. Good. I'm judging the chutney, and you're holding the spoons.

p1b-2.speaker: sam
p1b-2.text: Ma'am, I was told this was a day off.

p1b-3.speaker: quaile
p1b-3.text: It is. Nobody has ever been murdered over chutney.

p1c-1.speaker: gerald
p1c-1.text: Gerald Pike, chairman. The marrow results are delayed. Would whoever has moved the marrows please put them back.

p1c-2.speaker: gerald
p1c-2.text: And the vicar's cordial is in the church-hall flasks again. Do not take them home.

p1c-3.speaker: narrator
p1c-3.text: He has judged the marrows for thirty-one years. His own marrow has won for nine.

p1d-1.speaker: narrator
p1d-1.text: The scarecrow competition. This year's theme is Our Village: a straw vicar in a yellow jacket, a straw butcher, and a straw man in a panama hat.

p1d-2.speaker: narrator
p1d-2.text: The straw Gerald has a red rosette, and faces the wrong way.

p1d-3.speaker: narrator
p1d-3.text: Behind the produce tent, somebody screams. It is a short scream, and then a very English apology.

p2-open.speaker: narrator
p2-open.text: Gerald Pike is in a deckchair behind the produce tent, with his hat over his face. The woman who screamed is still apologising.

p2a-1.speaker: narrator
p2a-1.text: Half the show has followed you round the tent. The brass band has not stopped playing.

p2a-2.speaker: quaile
p2a-2.text: Keep them back, Sam. Use your height.

p2b-1.speaker: narrator
p2b-1.text: No pulse. His hand is cool. Under the hat his face is calm, as if somebody has just told him his marrow won.

p2b-2.speaker: quaile
p2b-2.text: Don't move him. Ring it in. Then look at what's on the grass.

p2c-1.speaker: narrator
p2c-1.text: A blue enamel flask, half full of something pale. A brown label on a string: Church Hall.

p2c-2.speaker: sam
p2c-2.text: He told everybody not to take them home.

p2c-3.speaker: quaile
p2c-3.text: Then why has he got one?

p2d-1.speaker: quaile
p2d-1.text: Seventy-two, heavy, red in the face, a hot day. The doctor will say heart.

p2d-3.speaker: quaile
p2d-3.text: I'll say a man who tells four hundred people not to touch the vicar's flasks doesn't drink from one. Find his wife.

p3-open.speaker: narrator
p3-open.text: Margaret Pike is in her garden, two fields from the show, deadheading roses. Nobody has told her. You have to.

p3a-1.speaker: sam
p3a-1.text: Mrs Pike, I'm sorry. Your husband has died.

p3a-4.speaker: margaret
p3a-4.text: He'd have wanted to be in front of it.

p3b-1.speaker: margaret
p3b-1.text: Gerald only drank from the green flask. Elderflower. He made it himself, and nobody else would touch it.

p3b-2.speaker: margaret
p3b-2.text: He forgot it this morning. He forgot it every morning, and I took it down to him at twelve.

p3b-4.speaker: margaret
p3b-4.text: Not today. I had the roses.

p3c-1.speaker: narrator
p3c-1.text: Red handles, clean blades. She wears them on a cord round her neck.

p3c-2.speaker: margaret
p3c-2.text: If you want to know whether I've cut any foxgloves, Sergeant, count them.

p3d-1.speaker: narrator
p3d-1.text: Forty-one foxgloves along the back wall. You count them twice. Every stem is standing.

p3d-2.speaker: narrator
p3d-2.text: At the end of the border stands the scarecrow in the panama hat. An hour ago it was at the show.

p4-open.speaker: narrator
p4-open.text: The marrow tent. Forty marrows on trestles, and one woman in a butcher's apron, who has not left.

p4a-1.speaker: narrator
p4a-1.text: Gerald's marrow is on the end of the table. This year it has no card.

p4a-2.speaker: dilys
p4a-2.text: He judged it himself. Every year. Nobody said anything, because it was Gerald.

p4b-1.speaker: dilys
p4b-1.text: Dilys Rudd, Rudd's Butchers. I didn't kill him, love. I was weighing.

p4b-2.speaker: quaile
p4b-2.text: I'm told he was going to disqualify you this year.

p4c-1.speaker: narrator
p4c-1.text: In her apron pocket, a veterinary syringe the size of a cucumber.

p4c-2.speaker: dilys
p4c-2.text: Water. Two pints a night, straight up the stalk. Every grower in this tent does it. Gerald just never caught anyone else.

p4d-1.speaker: narrator
p4d-1.text: Her marrow is weeping water from a hole the size of a pin. So is Gerald's.

p4d-3.speaker: dilys
p4d-3.text: Thirty-one years. Write that down, love. Big letters.

p5-open.speaker: narrator
p5-open.text: The car park is a field. Toby Pike is in the middle of it, on the phone, in suede loafers.

p5a-1.speaker: narrator
p5a-1.text: Range Rovers, a tractor, the brass band's minibus. Somebody has parked across the gate, and it is Toby.

p5b-1.speaker: toby
p5b-1.text: Sorry, sorry. Clients. Toby Pike, Pike and Lowe, Cirencester. Is it Dad?

p5b-3.speaker: toby
p5b-3.text: Right. Right. Is there a form for probate, or do I just ring someone?

p5c-1.speaker: toby
p5c-1.text: In the car, on a call to a man in Swindon from half one till twenty past two. He wants a barn.

p5c-2.speaker: narrator
p5c-2.text: His phone agrees. So does his dashcam, which has filmed him talking to the windscreen for fifty minutes.

p5c-3.speaker: quaile
p5c-3.text: Your father owned the fields behind the church.

p5c-4.speaker: toby
p5c-4.text: Forty houses, if the parish council sees sense. Dad wouldn't. I'm not hiding it.

p5d-1.speaker: narrator
p5d-1.text: There is mud to his ankles and no straw on him anywhere. He has not been near the produce tent.

p5d-2.speaker: narrator
p5d-2.text: In the back of the brass band's minibus, the straw vicar sits with its seatbelt on.

p6-open.speaker: narrator
p6-open.text: St Aldhelm's: the church, the hall, the vicarage, and a roof that has been under scaffolding since Easter.

p6a-1.speaker: clement
p6a-1.text: Sergeant! Inspector! Dreadful. I've been on the cake stall all afternoon, you can ask anyone.

p6b-1.speaker: narrator
p6b-1.text: The vicarage border: foxgloves, and six of them cut down to the stalk. Clean cuts, this week.

p6c-1.speaker: narrator
p6c-1.text: The church-hall kitchen. Seven hooks, numbered in marker pen. Six blue flasks.

p6c-2.speaker: clement
p6c-2.text: One always goes walkabout at the show. Gerald's very strict about it. Was.

p6d-1.speaker: narrator
p6d-1.text: The roof appeal board: a thermometer painted red up to eight thousand pounds. The target is sixty.

p6d-2.speaker: narrator
p6d-2.text: Someone has added four thousand in a brighter red, very recently, and it has run.

p7-open.speaker: narrator
p7-open.text: Gerald's study. Margaret lets you in, and stays in the doorway.

p7a-1.speaker: narrator
p7a-1.text: Rosettes on every wall, in date order from 1994. Out on the lawn, the scarecrow in the panama hat looks in at the window.

p7a-2.speaker: margaret
p7a-2.text: That wasn't there this morning either.

p7b-1.speaker: margaret
p7b-1.text: He kept the Society's books in there. He was treasurer before Clement, and he never forgave him for being better at it.

p7c-1.speaker: narrator
p7c-1.text: A notebook in Gerald's square capitals. Saturday's page: Prize fund four thousand short. Roof? Ask C. After marrows.

p7c-2.speaker: sam
p7c-2.text: After the marrows. He was going to ask him today.

p7c-3.speaker: quaile
p7c-3.text: And he never got past the marrows.

p7d-1.speaker: narrator
p7d-1.text: Nine silver cups. All of them the Pike Cup, all won by Gerald Pike, all judged by Gerald Pike.

p7d-2.speaker: quaile
p7d-2.text: I'd have poisoned him over that alone.

p7d-4.speaker: quaile
p7d-4.text: I'm deaf in one ear, Sam. I can say what I like.

p8-open.speaker: narrator
p8-open.text: The Plough, half past eight. The whole village is in, and pretending not to listen to you.

p8a-1.speaker: narrator
p8a-1.text: The blackboard by the door says Quiz cancelled, mark of respect. Under that, it says Scampi, nine pounds.

p8b-1.speaker: quaile
p8b-1.text: Go on, then. Who did it?

p8b-2.speaker: quaile
p8b-2.text: Foxglove's digitalis. On a hot day it stops a big man's heart, and it looks like a big man's heart on a hot day.

p8c-alibi.speaker: narrator
p8c-alibi.text: Toby, on the phone in a field for fifty minutes.

p8c-empty.speaker: narrator
p8c-empty.text: Your notebook has the date in it, and the word chutney.

p8c-flask.speaker: narrator
p8c-flask.text: A church-hall flask by his chair, and he never drank from them.

p8c-foxglove.speaker: narrator
p8c-foxglove.text: Six foxgloves cut at the vicarage. None cut at the Pikes'.

p8c-green.speaker: narrator
p8c-green.text: His own green flask was at home on the draining board.

p8c-notebook.speaker: narrator
p8c-notebook.text: Four thousand pounds short in the prize fund. Ask C.

p8c-syringe.speaker: narrator
p8c-syringe.text: Dilys and a syringe. Water, and only in marrows.

p8d-1.speaker: narrator
p8d-1.text: At the bar, between the darts team and the vet, the straw butcher has a pint in front of it. Nobody has drunk any.

p8d-2.speaker: quaile
p8d-2.text: Don't. It happens every year. Nobody owns up.

p9-open.speaker: narrator
p9-open.text: The village hall. The prize-giving goes ahead, because Gerald would have wanted it, says the vicar, who is giving the prizes.

p9a-1.speaker: clement
p9a-1.text: The Pike Cup for the heaviest marrow goes this year to Mrs Dilys Rudd.

p9a-2.speaker: narrator
p9a-2.text: Dilys does not go up. One by one, the hall turns round to look at you.

p9b-1.speaker: narrator
p9b-1.text: Margaret in the front row, very upright. Dilys with her arms folded. Toby at the back, on his phone.

p9c-1.speaker: narrator
p9c-1.text: The vicar holds the cup with both hands. The lid rattles.

p9e-flask.speaker: sam
p9e-flask.text: And he died with one of your flasks by his chair. He never drank from them. Somebody handed it to him.

p9e-foxglove.speaker: sam
p9e-foxglove.text: Six foxgloves cut in your garden. Not slugs.

p9e-hunch.speaker: sam
p9e-hunch.text: I can't prove it yet. But you offered us cordial.

p9e-notebook.speaker: sam
p9e-notebook.text: The prize fund was four thousand short, and the roof went up four thousand. Gerald wrote it down: ask C, after the marrows.

p9f-dilys.speaker: dilys
p9f-dilys.text: I put water in marrows, love. Not in men.

p9f-margaret.speaker: margaret
p9f-margaret.text: I had forty-one foxgloves this morning, Sergeant. I still have forty-one. You counted them.

p9f-toby.speaker: toby
p9f-toby.text: I was in a field with a man from Swindon. There's a video. It's very long.

p9g-1.speaker: quaile
p9g-1.text: Sit down, Sam. Vicar, the prize fund is four thousand short, and your roof is four thousand up. Gerald was going to say so, after the marrows.

p9h-1.speaker: clement
p9h-1.text: He was going to stand up here and say it. In front of everyone. In front of the roof.

p9h-2.speaker: clement
p9h-2.text: I only wanted him to be ill. For the afternoon.

p9h-3.speaker: quaile
p9h-3.text: The roof will still leak, Vicar.
